headline: US Judge Scraps 4-Year Cap; Indian Students Keep Full-Course Stay

image.author: 4300streetcar (own work, Wikimedia Commons)
image.subject: John Joseph Moakley United States Courthouse, Boston: seat of the US District Court for the District of Massachusetts, where Judge Saylor ruled

fact_sources.fact: US District Judge F. Dennis Saylor (Boston/Massachusetts) set aside/vacated the DHS rule on Monday 16 Nov 2026 (US time), calling it 'arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion'
Rule capped F (and J) stays at 4 years; students needing more time would have to apply to DHS for an extension; it would end 'duration of status'
Post-course grace period would have fallen from 60 days to 30 (F-1); 60-day grace remains
Foreign journalists' (I visa) stays would have been cut to 240 days
Judge said the rule would prevent extended study such as PhD programmes and bar joint degrees
Rule published in the Federal Register on 17 July 2026; a 14 Sept 2026 court order postponed it, so it never took effect
Government appealed the September order to the First Circuit (pending at the time of the ruling); the final ruling can also be appealed
3,63,019 Indian students in the US in 2024-25 (Open Doors 2025), more than any other country
